title: 100BB 6-Max GTO Preflop Ranges, 169 Starting Hands & 25 Canonical Matchup Benchmarks (2026)

startingHands.name: Pocket Aces
startingHands.summary: Pocket Aces (AA) Is The Strongest Starting Hand In No-Limit Texas Hold'em, Winning 85.2% Of Pots Against A Random Hand And Opening Or 4-Betting At 100% Frequency From Every Table Position.
startingHands.vs3Bet: 100% 4-Bet Value From Out Of Position; 85% 4-Bet And 15% Trap Call In Position At 100BB.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Build The Pot Across Three Streets On Dry And Disconnected Boards. On Monotone Or Four-To-A-Straight Boards, Check Back Or Bet Small When You Do Not Hold The Nut Suit Blocker.

startingHands.name: Pocket Kings
startingHands.summary: Pocket Kings (KK) Is The Second-Best Starting Hand In Texas Hold'em With 82.4% Equity Against A Random Hand, Playing As A Pure Open-Raise, 3-Bet, And 4-Bet Value Hand Across 100BB Stacks.
startingHands.vs3Bet: 100% 4-Bet Value Across Standard 100BB 6-Max Configurations.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Value Bet Aggressively On King-High And Under-Card Flops. When An Ace Falls On The Flop (Approximately 22.6% Of The Time), Shift To Pot Control And Check-Call Against Uncapped Ranges.

startingHands.name: Pocket Queens
startingHands.summary: Pocket Queens (QQ) Ranks Third Among All 169 Hold'em Starting Hands With 79.9% Heads-Up Equity Vs. A Random Hand And A 53.5% Edge In Classic Coinflips Against Ace-King Suited.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Mix 65% 4-Bet And 35% Call Vs. Early Position 3-Bets; 100% 4-Bet Value Vs. Button And Blind 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Push Equity On Low And Medium Boards Before Overcards Arrive. Exercise Caution Facing Multiple Barrels On Ace-High Or King-High Textures.

startingHands.name: Pocket Jacks
startingHands.summary: Pocket Jacks (JJ) Is The Fourth-Ranked Starting Hand In Texas Hold'em, Opening 100% From Every Position While Mixing Calls And 3-Bets Against Tight Early-Position Opens.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call 70% And 4-Bet 30% In Position; Call Or 4-Bet Depending On Villain 3-Bet Frequency Out Of Position.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Overcards (Q, K, Or A) Appear On The Flop 57% Of The Time. Bet For Value And Protection When JJ Remains An Overpair, And Use Suit Blockers To Guide Bluff-Catching On Overcard Boards.

startingHands.name: Pocket Tens
startingHands.summary: Pocket Tens (TT) Bridges The Gap Between Premium Overpairs And Set-Mining Medium Pairs, Winning 75.1% Against A Random Hand And Opening 100% Across All 6-Max Positions.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Primarily Call 3-Bets In Position To Retain Dominated Broadways; Mix 4-Bet All-In At 25BB To 40BB Tournament Stacks.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Play As A Strong Value Overpair On Nine-High And Lower Flops, While Using Ten Blockers To Straight Combinations On Broadway Textures.

startingHands.name: Ace-King Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-King Suited (AKs) Is The Strongest Non-Paired Hand In Texas Hold'em, Combining Top-Pair Nut Kicker Strength With Nut Flush And Royal Flush Potential Plus Key AA And KK Card Removal.
startingHands.vs3Bet: 100% 4-Bet Or Call Mix; Ideal 4-Bet Jam Hand Because It Blocks Half Of Villain's AA And KK Combinations.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Continuation Bet High Cards And Backdoor Nut Flush Draws Aggressively. When Hitting Top Pair Top Kicker, Extract Three Streets Of Value Against Worse Top Pairs.

startingHands.name: Ace-King Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Ace-King Offsuit (AKo) Accounts For 12 Combinations (Three Times As Frequent As AKs) And Serves As The Primary High-Volume 3-Bet And 4-Bet Value/Bluff-Blocker Hand In GTO Ranges.
startingHands.vs3Bet: High-Frequency 4-Bet Because Realizing Equity Out Of Position Unimproved Is Harder Than Pushing Fold Equity Preflop.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Dominates Single-Raised And 3-Bet Pots When Hitting An Ace Or King. Unimproved On Low Connected Boards, Prefer Checking Or Using Nut Blockers Selectively.

startingHands.name: Ace-Queen Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Queen Suited (AQs) Opens 100% From Every Position And Functions As A Core 3-Bet Value Hand From Middle And Late Positions With Strong Postflop Playability.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call 75% And 4-Bet 25% In Position; Call Or Fold Vs. Tight Early-Position 4-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Value Bet Two Streets Comfortably On Ace-High And Queen-High Flops While Utilizing Nut Flush Draws For Semi-Bluff Check-Raises.

startingHands.name: Ace-Queen Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Ace-Queen Offsuit (AQo) Is A 100% Open-Raise Across All 6-Max Positions That Requires Disciplined 3-Bet Defense To Avoid Reverse Implied Odds Against AK And AA/KK/QQ.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Or Call Mix Vs. Early Position 3-Bets; Call Or 4-Bet Bluff Vs. Wide Late-Position 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Extract Value From Worse Aces (AJ, AT) In Single-Raised Pots, And Control Pot Size When Facing Heavy Action In 3-Bet Pots.

startingHands.name: Ace-Jack Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Jack Suited (AJs) Opens 100% From Every 6-Max Seat And Provides High Nut-Flush And Broadway Straight Playability In Both Single-Raised And 3-Bet Pots.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position To Realize Suited Nut Equity; Mix Fold And Call Out Of Position Against Tight 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Leverage Backdoor And Direct Nut Flush Draws As Aggressive Semi-Bluffs While Pot-Controlling One-Pair Hands On Wet Boards.

startingHands.name: Ace-Five Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Five Suited (A5s) Is The Premier GTO 3-Bet And 4-Bet Bluff Hand In Modern Poker Because It Blocks Pocket Aces While Retaining Nut Flush And Wheel Straight (A-2-3-4-5) Equity When Called.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Primary 4-Bet Bluff Candidate Against Cutoff And Button 3-Bets Due To Ace Card Removal And Playability.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Barrel Aggressively With Nut Flush Draws And Wheel Gutshots. Avoid Calling Multiple Streets With Weak Top Pair No Kicker.

startingHands.name: King-Queen Suited
startingHands.summary: King-Queen Suited (KQs) Opens 100% From Every Position And Flops Top Pair, Flush Draws, Or Open-Ended Straight Draws At One Of The Highest Rates In The Deck.
startingHands.vs3Bet: High-Frequency Call In Position; Mix Call And 4-Bet Bluff Out Of Position.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Dominates KJs, KTs, QJs, And QTs When Hitting Top Pair. Apply Maximum Pressure With Royal And Broadway Combo Draws.

startingHands.name: Queen-Jack Suited
startingHands.summary: Queen-Jack Suited (QJs) Is A Premier Suited Broadway Connector Opening 100% Across All 6-Max Positions With Exceptional Multiway And Single-Raised Postflop Playability.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position When Deep-Stacked (100BB+) Because Suited Connected Hands Realize Equity Above Raw All-In Percentages.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Attack Broadway-Heavy And Middling Connected Boards Using Straight And Flush Draw Equity.

startingHands.name: Jack-Ten Suited
startingHands.summary: Jack-Ten Suited (JTs) Can Make Four Distinct Nut Straights (8-9-T-J-Q Through T-J-Q-K-A), Making It The Highest-Playability Suited Connector In Deep-Stack No-Limit Hold'em.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Profitable Call In Position At 100BB+; Mix Polarized 3-Bets From The Button And Blinds.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Semi-Bluff Relentlessly When Flopping 12+ Out Combo Draws (Flush Draw Plus Open-Ended Straight Draw Holds Over 54% Equity Vs. Overpairs).

startingHands.name: Ten-Nine Suited
startingHands.summary: Ten-Nine Suited (T9s) Opens At High Frequency Across All 6-Max Positions And Excels At Cracking Big Overpairs By Flopping Disguised Two-Pairs, Trips, Straights, And Flushes.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position When Effective Stacks Offer Sufficient Implied Odds (100BB+).
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Prioritize Aggressive Check-Raises And Turn Barrels When Picking Up Double-Gutter Or Open-Ended Straight Plus Flush Draws.

startingHands.name: Pocket Nines
startingHands.summary: Pocket Nines (99) Wins 72.1% Against A Random Hand, Opens 100% From All 6-Max Positions, And Is A Slight Favorite Over Two Overcards Like AKo (54.3% Vs. 45.3%).
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position For Set Value And Mid-Board Showdown Equity; High-EV 20BB-30BB Tournament Reshove Hand.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Bet For Value And Protection On Low Disconnected Boards, And Transition To Set-Mining And Bluff-Catching On Broadway-Heavy Textures.

startingHands.name: Pocket Eights
startingHands.summary: Pocket Eights (88) Opens 100% From Every 6-Max Seat At 100BB And Flops A Set Approximately 11.8% Of The Time (7.5 To 1 Against) With Strong Implied Odds Against Overpairs.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call When Implied Odds Satisfy The Set-Mining Threshold (Call <= 7% To 10% Of Effective Stack).
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Fast-Play Flopped Sets On Wet Boards To Deny Equity And Charge Overpairs Maximum Chips.

startingHands.name: Pocket Sevens
startingHands.summary: Pocket Sevens (77) Marks The Bottom Of The Pure 100% UTG Opening Pocket Pairs In 6-Max 100BB GTO Solutions, Combining 66.2% Raw Equity With Disguised Set-Mining Value.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Set-Mine In Position When Stacks Are Deep; Fold Out Of Position Against Large 3-Bet Sizing.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Check-Call Single Small Bets On Dry High-Card Flops And Pile Chips In When Turning Or Flopping Three Of A Kind.

startingHands.name: Pocket Deuces
startingHands.summary: Pocket Deuces (22) Is A 51.6% Favorite Preflop Against Unpaired Overcards Like Ace-King Offsuit, But Requires Set-Mining Discipline Postflop Because Every Board Card Is An Overcard.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Unless Deep-Stacked In Position With At Least 15-To-1 Implied Odds.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Follow The "No Set, No Bet" Baseline In Multiway Pots While Disguising Bottom Set On Ace-High And King-High Boards.

startingHands.name: Seven-Deuce Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Seven-Deuce Offsuit (72o) Is Mathematically The Worst Starting Hand In Texas Hold'em (Rank 169 Of 169, 34.6% Equity Vs. Random) Because It Cannot Make A Single Five-Card Straight Using Both Hole Cards And Has Zero Flush Potential.
startingHands.vs3Bet: 100% Pure Fold Unless Playing A Special Seven-Deuce Bounty Prop Game With Sufficient Table Bounty Overlay.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: In Standard Games, Fold Preflop 100% Of The Time. In Seven-Deuce Bounty Games, Calculate The Total Table Bounty Pool Relative To The Effective Stack Before Attempting Pre-Flop Or Flop Bluffs.

startingHands.name: Pocket Sixes
startingHands.summary: Pocket Sixes (66) Holds 63.3% Equity Against A Random Hand And Opens At High Frequency Across All 6-Max Positions, Excelling At Set-Mining And Blocking Wheel Straight Completions.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position With Deep Implied Odds; Fold Out Of Position At 100BB.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Look To Flop Sets Or Open-Ended Straight Draws On Low Runouts (5-4-3, 6-5-2) And Check-Fold Unimproved On Heavy Broadway Textures.

startingHands.name: Pocket Fives
startingHands.summary: Pocket Fives (55) Is The Highest Wheel-Connected Small Pocket Pair (60.3% Equity Vs. Random), Capable Of Participating In Both Ace-To-Five And Five-To-Nine Straight Boards While Flopping Disguised Sets.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position Only When Implied Odds Justify Set-Mining; High-EV Re-Steal Jam At 18BB To 22BB Tournament Stacks.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Capitalize On Disguised Sets And Double-Gutter Straight Draws On Low Wheel Flops (A-4-3, 6-4-2).

startingHands.name: Pocket Fours
startingHands.summary: Pocket Fours (44) Carries 57.0% Equity Against A Random Hand And Functions Primarily As A Positional Set-Mining Hand In 100BB Cash Games And A Profitable Push-Fold Jam Hand Below 20BB.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Out Of Position; Call In Position Only Against Large Stack Depths.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Fast-Play Flopped Sets On Dynamic Wet Boards To Charge Flush And Straight Draws Before Turn Scare Cards Freeze Action.

startingHands.name: Pocket Threes
startingHands.summary: Pocket Threes (33) Wins 53.7% Against A Random Hand And Opens Pure From Cutoff, Button, And Small Blind At 100BB To Target Disguised Bottom Sets Against Top-Pair Heavy Ranges.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Facing 3-Bets Unless Deep-Stacked In Position.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Play Strictly For Set Value Or Low Wheel Board Coverage; Check-Fold Unimproved On Multiple Overcard Runouts.

startingHands.name: Ace-Ten Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Ten Suited (ATs) Combines Nut-Flush Potential, Broadway Straight Connectivity, And Ace Blocker Power, Opening 100% From Every 6-Max Seat With 64.7% Equity Against A Random Hand.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position Against Standard 3-Bets And Use As A High-EV 3-Bet Against Cutoff And Button Opens.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Barrel Nut Flush Draws And Broadway Gutshots Aggressively While Exercising Pot Control On Ace-High Boards Against Early-Position Openers.

startingHands.name: King-Jack Suited
startingHands.summary: King-Jack Suited (KJs) Is A High-Playability Suited Broadway Hand (62.6% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens 100% Across All 6-Max Positions And Frequently Flops Second-Nut Flush Draws And Royal Flush Draws.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB; Mix 3-Bet For Value And Equity Denial From The Blinds Against Late-Position Steals.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Apply Pressure On King-High, Jack-High, And Queen-Ten-X Boards While Avoiding 3-Street All-In Commit Spots With Unimproved One-Pair Against Uncapped Ranges.

startingHands.name: Eight-Seven Suited
startingHands.summary: Eight-Seven Suited (87s) Is A Premier Middle Suited Connector (53.9% Equity Vs. Random) Used By Solvers As A Mixed Early-Position Open And Polarized 3-Bet To Ensure Board Coverage On Medium-And-Low Runouts.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB+ To Realize Disguised Straight, Flush, And Two-Pair Equity.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Semi-Bluff Aggressively With Combo Draws (Open-Ended Straight Draw Plus Flush Draw) Which Hold Over 54% Equity Even Against Pocket Aces.

startingHands.name: Ace-Nine Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Nine Suited (A9s) Is The Strongest Non-Broadway Suited Ace (63.0% Equity Vs. Random), Opening As A Low-Frequency Mix From Early Position And 100% From Hijack, Cutoff, Button, And Small Blind.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call Selectively In Position Against Wide Late-Position 3-Bets; Fold Facing Tight Early-Position 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Exercise Pot Control On Ace-High Boards Against Early-Position Openers Where Stronger Kicker Aces Dominate, And Barrel Aggressively When Flopping Nut Flush Draws.

startingHands.name: Ace-Four Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Four Suited (A4s) Is A Prime Suited Wheel Ace (60.3% Equity Vs. Random) Used Across All 6-Max Positions As An Open-Raise And Polarized 3-Bet Or 4-Bet Bluff Blocking Pocket Aces.
startingHands.vs3Bet: High-Frequency 4-Bet Bluff Candidate Holding The Ace Blocker And Nut Flush Plus Wheel Straight Playability.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Attack Low Connected Boards (5-3-2, 6-5-3) And Use Nut Flush Draws As High-Equity Multi-Street Semi-Bluffs.

startingHands.name: Ace-Three Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Three Suited (A3s) Is A Versatile Suited Wheel Ace (59.4% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens Pure From Hijack Through Small Blind And Serves As A Polarized 3-Bet Bluff Against Late-Position Opens.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Mix Call In Position Against Button/Blind 3-Bets And Occasional 4-Bet Bluff; Fold Out Of Position Vs. Tight 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Prioritize Nut Flush Draw And Wheel Gutshot Semi-Bluffs Rather Than Calling Down Multi-Street Bets With Weak Top Pair.

startingHands.name: Ace-Two Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Two Suited (A2s) Completes The Core Suited Wheel Ace Quartet (58.5% Equity Vs. Random), Offering Nut-Flush Equity And Five-High Straight Potential From Middle And Late Positions.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call Selectively In Position Deep-Stacked Or Use As A Polarized 3-Bet From The Blinds Against Cutoff And Button Steals.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Realize Equity Cheaply In Position And Apply Maximum Pressure When Turning Or Rivering The Nut Flush Or Disguised Wheel.

startingHands.name: Ace-Jack Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Ace-Jack Offsuit (AJo) Is A High-Card Broadway Hand (63.6% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens At Mixed Frequency Under The Gun And 100% From Middle And Late Positions While Requiring Discipline Against 3-Bets.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Facing Early-And-Middle Position 3-Bets Due To Reverse Implied Odds Against AK And AQ; Defend In Blind-Vs-Button Spots.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Extract Value From Worse Aces And Second Pairs In Single-Raised Pots While Avoiding Three-Street Stacks Off On Unimproved One-Pair Boards.

startingHands.name: King-Queen Offsuit
startingHands.summary: King-Queen Offsuit (KQo) Is The Strongest Non-Ace Offsuit Hand (61.5% Equity Vs. Random), Opening At 35% Frequency From UTG And 100% From Hijack, Cutoff, Button, And Small Blind.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call Or 3-Bet In Late Position Versus Button/Cutoff Opens; Fold Facing Tight Early-Position 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Value Bet Top Pair With Strong Kicker Across Two Streets In Single-Raised Pots And Use Broadway Blockers To Bluff River Runouts.

startingHands.name: King-Ten Suited
startingHands.summary: King-Ten Suited (KTs) Is A High-Connectivity Suited Broadway Hand (61.8% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens Across All 6-Max Positions And Flops Strong Second-Nut Flush Draws And Broadway Straight Draws.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB Against Standard 3-Bets And Use As A Linear 3-Bet From The Blinds Versus Button Opens.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Play Aggressively With Combo Draws (Queen-Jack-X And Ace-Jack-X Boards) While Controlling Pot Size With Top Pair Ten-Kicker.

startingHands.name: Queen-Ten Suited
startingHands.summary: Queen-Ten Suited (QTs) Is A Dynamic Suited Broadway Gapper (60.1% Equity Vs. Random) Capable Of Making Broadway, King-High, And Queen-High Straights Alongside Strong Flush Draws.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB Stack Depth Due To Superior Equity Realization; Mix 3-Bet From Cutoff And Button.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Leverage Double-Gutshot And Open-Ended Straight Draws On Broadway And Middle Boards To Pressure One-Pair Holdings.

startingHands.name: Seven-Six Suited
startingHands.summary: Seven-Six Suited (76s) Is A Classic Middle Suited Connector (52.2% Equity Vs. Random) That Maximizes Board Coverage On Low-And-Medium Runouts And Crushes Overpairs When Flopping Disguised Two-Pairs And Straights.
startingHands.vs3Bet: High-EV Call In Position At 100BB+ And Low-Frequency Polarized 3-Bet Bluff To Prevent Opponents From Capping Your Range On Low Boards.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Fast-Play Combo Draws And Check-Raise Low Connected Flops (8-5-4, 9-8-2) Where Pre-Flop Raisers Hold Unimproved Overcards.

startingHands.name: Six-Five Suited
startingHands.summary: Six-Five Suited (65s) Is The Lowest Zero-Gap Suited Connector Without Wheel Card Domination (50.8% Equity Vs. Random), Frequently Included In Solver UTG Mixed Opens And Polarized 3-Bet Ranges.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call Deep-Stacked In Position Or Use As A Deceptive Polarized 3-Bet Bluff With Clean Straight And Flush Outs.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Capitalize On Hidden Nut Advantage On 4-3-2, 7-4-3, And 8-7-4 Textures While Folding Unimproved Single Pairs Against Heavy Action.

startingHands.name: Ace-Eight Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Eight Suited (A8s) Is A Middle Suited Ace (60.9% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens Profitably From Hijack Through Small Blind And Realizes Strong Nut-Flush Equity Across Multiway And Heads-Up Pots.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position Against Cutoff And Button 3-Bets Or Mix As A Blocker 4-Bet Bluff.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Play Pot-Controlled One-Street Or Two-Street Value When Flopping Top Pair Weak Kicker, And Barrel Aggressively When Turning Or Flopping Nut Flush Draws.

startingHands.name: Ace-Seven Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Seven Suited (A7s) Is A Flexible Suited Ace (59.9% Equity Vs. Random) That Combines Top-Of-Deck Ace Blockers With Nut Flush Draw Potential And Backdoor Straight Connectivity Across 6-Max Ranges.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Defend In Position Versus Late-Position 3-Bets And Fold Against Tight Early-Position 3-Bet Ranges.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Check Back Ace-High Flops In Position To Prevent Self-Isolation Against Stronger Aces, While Semibluffing Relentlessly With Four-Flush Boards.

startingHands.name: Ace-Six Suited
startingHands.summary: Ace-Six Suited (A6s) Is The Bridge Between Middle And Wheel Suited Aces (58.9% Equity Vs. Random), Opening Standard From Cutoff, Button, And Small Blind While Mixing From Early Seats.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Out Of Position Against Linear 3-Bets; Mix Call And Polarized 4-Bet Bluffs In Late Position.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Focus On Realizing Nut Flush Equity And Picking Up Low-Board Backdoor Straight Draws On 5-4-X And 7-5-X Textures.

startingHands.name: Ace-Ten Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Ace-Ten Offsuit (ATo) Is A High-Card Offsuit Broadway Holding (63.5% Equity Vs. Random Across 12 Combinations) That Dominates Late-Position Stealing Ranges And Short-Stack Push-Fold Spots.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Against Early And Middle Position 3-Bets; Mix Call Or 4-Bet Bluff Only In Wide Button Vs. Blind Battles.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Extract Thin Value Against Worse One-Pair Hands In Late-Position Pots While Avoiding Three-Street Stacks Off On Single-Pair Ace Boards.

startingHands.name: King-Jack Offsuit
startingHands.summary: King-Jack Offsuit (KJo) Is A Staple Late-Position Offsuit Broadway Hand (60.4% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens Pure From Cutoff, Button, And Small Blind But Requires Discipline Against 3-Bets.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Primarily Fold Facing 3-Bets Due To Reverse Implied Odds Against AK, AQ, AJ, And KQ.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Bet For Value On King-High And Jack-High Textures In Single-Raised Pots, And Use Broadway Blockers To Bluff River Runouts When Draws Miss.

startingHands.name: Queen-Jack Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Queen-Jack Offsuit (QJo) Is A Connected Offsuit Broadway Hand (58.2% Equity Vs. Random) That Flops Frequent Open-Ended Straight Draws And Top Pairs In Late-Position Steal Scenarios.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Facing 3-Bets Out Of Position And Against Tight Opponents; Defend Selectively In Big Blind Single-Raised Pots.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Play Straight Draws Aggressively On Ten-Nine-X And King-Ten-X Boards While Pot-Controlling Vulnerable Top Pair Jack-Kicker Hands.

startingHands.name: Jack-Ten Offsuit
startingHands.summary: Jack-Ten Offsuit (JTo) Boasts The Highest Straight Connectivity Of Any Offsuit Hand (55.4% Equity Vs. Random), Making Four Different Nut Straights Across 8-9-Q, 9-Q-K, And Q-K-A Runouts.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold To 3-Bets Outside Of Deep-Stacked Button Vs. Blind Configurations.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Prioritize High-Equity Straight Draws Over Weak One-Pair Showdown Value, And Leverage Nut Straight Advantage On Queen-Nine-Eight Textures.

startingHands.name: King-Nine Suited
startingHands.summary: King-Nine Suited (K9s) Is A High-Card Suited One-Gapper (59.5% Equity Vs. Random) That Opens Standard From Hijack Through Small Blind And Defends Profitably In The Big Blind.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position Against Wide Late-Position 3-Bets And Fold Against Early-Position 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Capitalize On Second-Nut Flush Draws And Jack-Ten-X Straight Draws While Checking Back Medium-Strength Top Pairs On Wet Boards.

startingHands.name: Queen-Nine Suited
startingHands.summary: Queen-Nine Suited (Q9s) Is A Versatile Suited One-Gapper (57.9% Equity Vs. Random) That Connects Strongly With Middle-And-High Flops (J-T-8, K-J-T) And Realizes Flush Equity Efficiently.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB Against Aggressive Button And Blind 3-Bettors.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Semi-Bluff Combo Draws And Double-Gutshots Aggressively While Using Queen Blockers To Catch Bluffs On Brick Rivers.

startingHands.name: Jack-Nine Suited
startingHands.summary: Jack-Nine Suited (J9s) Is One Of The Highest-Realization Suited One-Gappers In Hold'em (56.4% Equity Vs. Random), Famous For Flopping Disguised Straights On Q-T-8, T-8-7, And K-Q-T Boards.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position At 100BB Stack Depth Because Of Uncapped Straight And Flush Potential.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Apply Maximum Pressure When Flopping Open-Ended Or Double-Belly-Buster Straight Draws Paired With Backdoor Or Live Flush Equity.

startingHands.name: Ten-Eight Suited
startingHands.summary: Ten-Eight Suited (T8s) Is A Versatile Suited One-Gapper With 54.2% Equity Against A Random Hand That Flops Disguised Open-Ended And Double-Gutshot Straights Across Connected Middling Boards.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Call In Position Against Standard 3-Bet Sizings At 100BB+ Depth; Fold Out Of Position Against Early-Position 3-Bets.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Semi-Bluff Aggressively On 9-7-X, J-9-X, And Flush-Draw Boards Where Opponents Cap Their Ranges With Vulnerable One-Pair Hands.

startingHands.name: Nine-Seven Suited
startingHands.summary: Nine-Seven Suited (97s) Is A High-Playability Suited One-Gapper (52.1% Equity Vs. Random) That Connects Strongly With Low-To-Middling Boards (T-8-6, 8-6-5) Where Broadway Ranges Whiff.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Out Of Position; Mix Calls In Position Only At Deep 100BB+ Effective Stacks.
startingHands.postflopPlaybook: Leverage Nut Advantage On 8-6-X And T-8-X Textures By Check-Raising Combo Draws And Double-Barreling Turn Cards That Increase Straight Equity.

startingHands.name: Eight-Six Suited
startingHands.summary: Eight-Six Suited (86s) Is A Deceptive Late-Position Suited One-Gapper (50.1% Equity Vs. Random) Capable Of Cracking Overpairs When Flopping Hidden Straights On 9-7-5 And 7-5-4 Boards.
startingHands.vs3Bet: Fold Facing Standard 3-Bets Unless Deep-Stacked In Position Against Polarized Sizing.

flopShifts.equityShift: AA Drops To 8.4% Equity Vs Top Set KK; AA Must Rely On Two Remaining Aces Or Running Broadway.

flopShifts.handAAction: Bet Small 25% To 33% Pot Across All Three Streets To Extract Maximum Value From Underpair Kings.
flopShifts.equityShift: AA Locks Up 98.9% Equity With Top Set While KK Needs Running Kings For Quads (1.1% Equity).

flopShifts.handAAction: Bet 50% To 66% Pot For Value And Denial; Stack Off Unexploitably At Low Stack-To-Pot Ratios.
flopShifts.equityShift: AA Holds 80.5% Equity While KK Retains 19.5% Via Two King Outs And Backdoor Flush Draws.

evAnalysis.cash100bb: Pure 100% 4-Bet And 5-Bet All-In Value For Both AA And KK In 6-Max Cash Games. Folding KK Preflop At 100BB Against Any Balanced Range Is A Massive Mathematical Blunder.
evAnalysis.cash200bb: AA Remains A 100% 5-Bet All-In Value Hand. KK Still 4-Bets For Value, Though Against Ultra-Tight UTG 5-Bet Shoves At 200BB+ Some Solvers Mix Flat-Calling KK In Position.

evAnalysis.icmFinalTable: AA Never Folds Under Any Final Table ICM Pressure. KK Only Considers Folding In Extreme Satellite Bubble Scenarios Where Multiple Short Stacks Are Already All-In.

faqs.q: How Often Does Pocket Kings Beat Pocket Aces Preflop?
faqs.a: Across All 1,712,304 Possible Five-Card Board Runouts, Pocket Kings Wins Outright 17.59% Of The Time And Ties 0.46% Of The Time, Giving KK 17.82% Total Equity Against AA.

faqs.q: Should You Ever Fold KK Preflop In A 100BB Cash Game?
faqs.a: No. In 100BB 6-Max And 9-Max Cash Games, Balanced 4-Bet And 5-Bet Ranges Contain AKs, AKo, QQ, And Bluffs Like A5s, Giving KK Well Over 55% Equity Against An Opponent Stack-Off Range.

faqs.q: How Do Shared Suits Affect AA Vs KK Equity?
faqs.a: When AA And KK Share The Exact Same Two Suits, AA Equity Rises To 82.65% Because AA Blocks Both Of KK Backdoor Flush Draws.

flopShifts.equityShift: AKs Drops To 26.8% Equity With Six Overcard Outs Across Turn And River.

faqs.q: Why Is AKs Vs QQ Called A Coinflip If QQ Wins 53.9% Of The Time?
faqs.a: Because Both Hands Are Within 4% Of 50/50 Equity And Dead Blinds Plus 3-Bet Chips In The Center Make Both Sides +EV To Commit All-In At 100BB.

faqs.q: How Often Does AKs Hit An Ace Or King By The River?
faqs.a: With Six Unblocked Outs, AKs Pairs Either Its Ace Or Its King On The Board Approximately 48.7% Of The Time By The River.

faqs.a: Although JJ Is A 56.85% Preflop Favorite Against AKo, An Ace, King, Or Queen Lands On The Flop 51.8% Of The Time, Making Postflop Navigation Difficult When Not All-In Preflop.

faqs.q: How Many Combinations Of AKo Exist Compared To JJ?
faqs.a: There Are 12 Combinations Of AKo And Only 6 Combinations Of JJ, Meaning You Encounter AKo Twice As Frequently As Pocket Jacks.

faqs.q: Does JJ Gain Equity If It Shares A Suit With AKo?
